title: Homogenise a sample in a Dounce: ten full strokes of the tight pestle, head kept under the liquid, mortar held still
instruction: Homogenise the sample in the Dounce with ten full strokes of the pestle: each stroke down to the bottom and back up, keeping the pestle's head under the liquid, and hold the mortar still.
context: Dounce homogenisation is the standard hand method for lysing cells and isolating nuclei or organelles in biochemistry and cell-biology labs; protocols say exactly this: ten strokes of the tight pestle, slowly, never lifting the head out of the liquid (air foams and denatures the sample). The difficulty is physical: the tight pestle (0.05 mm clearance in a 10 mm bore) is a piston that meets a few newtons of drag down and suction up, which lifts the light mortar unless the other hand holds it; every stroke must reach the floor and rise at least 25 mm but stop before the head clears the liquid (38-43 mm, set by the trial's volume): a 13-18 mm window, ten times. Pulling faster than ~50 mm/s cavitates. Unlike valve metering (the burette titration task TK-688YJC), this is stroke force and travel with a hold.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table top (x forward, y left, z up); arms in the ready pose. Nalgene Unwire test-tube rack for 13 mm tubes (5970-0213, yellow acetal, 200 x 102 x 57 mm), long side along y, centred at x 30, y 0, on a silicone bench mat. In its centre hole stands a DWK Wheaton 357542 7 mL borosilicate Dounce mortar (grinding tube 13 mm OD, 10 mm bore, 82 mm long, 20 mm reservoir on top), bottom on the rack's base, axis at x 30, y 0. The tight (B) glass pestle (10 mm head, 6 mm shaft, 14 mm knob, 175 mm long) rests in it with the head on the floor; knob top 18 cm above the table. Sample: 3.0-3.4 mL (set by the seed) of water with 0.1% dish detergent. Nitrile cots on the finger pads. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: Latched over the whole trial, any one gives 0: the mortar rises more than 5 mm off the rack's base (video, tape mark on the reservoir level with the rack's top); it tips past 20 degrees (video); the head is pulled up out of the grinding tube into the reservoir (video through the glass). Otherwise: +0.08 per full stroke (head within 3 mm of the floor, then at least 25 mm above it, then back to the floor; tape marks on the tube at 3 and 25 mm), up to 10 (0.8); +0.2 once all ten are done if the foam on the sample at the end is under 2 mm (photo against a ruler); -0.05 per upstroke on which the head rose above the liquid and drew air (video: head above the meniscus). Floored at 0. Success = 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift the pestle out, empty and rinse the mortar and pestle with water, shake dry. Pipette the next seed's volume (3.0-3.4 mL, printed in the log) of 0.1% detergent water into the mortar, slide the tight pestle in slowly until the head rests on the floor, wipe the outside dry, stand the mortar in the marked hole. About 1 minute.
fidelity: Approximate. Rack fixed. The Dounce is a floating articulation: mortar (35 g) root, pestle (15 g) on a prismatic joint standing in for the 0.05 mm fit (no tilt or turn). The liquid's drag is the joint's damping (160 N s/m, ~8 N at 50 mm/s), equal and opposite on pestle and mortar, so a pull lifts an unheld mortar. No fluid simulation: liquid level, air drawn in, cavitation and foam come from a quasi-static volume model; constants estimated.
